# Vijaya Sutta (Snp 1.11 (PTS Snp 34))

**ID:** Snp 1.11 (PTS Snp 34)
**Section:** Suttanipāta (snp)

**Title (Pali):** Vijaya Sutta

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Vijaya Sutta* ("Victory", Sn 1.11, verses 193–206) is the eleventh discourse of the *Uragavagga* in the *Suttanipāta* [Hinüber 1996; Barua 1921]. In Burmese and manuscript traditions it also bears the alternative title *Kāmavicchandanikasutta* (or *Vicchindanikasutta*) [Bendall 1893; Katre 1931]. In the commentary *Paramatthajotikā II*, an unusual double *uppatti* (occasion of delivery) is postulated for this text [Hinüber 1996].

Pali-internal text reuse identified by DharmaNexus shows extensive sharing of verses with the *Nīti-gantha-saṅgaho Caturārakkhadīpanī* (§1.3–14.4), the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (§2.2–7.4), and the *Ekakanipāta-ṭīkā* of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language machine alignments connect its anatomical and cemetery motifs to Sanskrit and Tibetan texts treating *asubha* contemplations, such as the Sanskrit *Arthaviniścayasūtra*, *Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā*, and *Patna Dharmapada*, the Tibetan *Śikṣāsamuccaya* (D3940) and *Aṣṭādaśasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā* (D0010), as well as a parallel bodily-orifice contemplation in the Chinese *Ekottarika-āgama* (T 125) [DharmaNexus; Anālayo 2014].
